newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end down but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end down but off lows.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended lower on Friday due to continued profit-taking in several blue-chips despite rises in some first-tier banking stocks, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index closed down 3.15 points, or 0.47 percent, at 666.84 points, off an earlier low of 663.07 points. Compared with last Friday's close of 683.81 points, the index was down 2.5 percent, or 16.97 points, on the week.
Losers led gainers by 72 to 43, with 56 counters unchanged.
Brokers said improved sentiment on some bank issues failed to push the index up because of overall weakness.
News that the central bank, Bank Indonesia, had curbed loan growth triggered heavy selling in banking stocks in the last two days.
"But some investors bought back bank issues as loan growth was not the only key value driver for the banks," the analyst said.
He added that under the currently soft interest rate environment, the banks would be able to cut their deposit rates faster than their lending rates.
First-tier banking issues which were targeted by bargain hunters included Bank Negara Indonesia, Bank International Indonesia, Lippo Bank and Bank Pikko.
Continued selling in several blue-chips such as noodle maker Indofood, cigarette maker Sampoerna and its competitor Gudang Garam had kept the index from rebounding, brokers said.

Brokers said news that Sampoerna's president director had bought a 5.63 percent stake in Indofood and has a long term plan to hold 15 percent stake in the firm also contributed to weak sentiment in Sampoerna.
Shares of timber firm Barito Pacific eased after its unit on Friday signed a $991 million loan for a new pulp mill.

"Rumours that its subsidiary secured a foreign loan had been spread for the last two days. Today, investors just liquidated their profits after the news was confirmed," a broker with a foreign firm said.
